notes: kb/Work PB5070 holds the mechanism (the PADDING CHARACTER clause is a grammar rule no binder reads); it lists SR1 and SR3 of this clause, not this rule id. §1985:VII.2.7.3 SR2: "Data-name-1 may be qualified." Implemented at 85: paddingCharacterClause takes a dataReference, whose syntax admits IN and OF qualifiers, and VisitPaddingCharacterClause is the edition arm (accepted at --std 85 and 2002, COBOL0902 from 2014), so the qualified form the rule permits compiles; the witness writes PAD-CHAR OF PAD-GROUP-A where PAD-CHAR is defined in two groups. Not implemented: the qualification itself. Nothing resolves data-name-1 (the clause is parsed and ignored, the grammar comment says so), so the qualifiers are never applied: at --std 85 PAD-CHAR OF NO-SUCH-GROUP, an item qualified by a group it is not in, the unqualified PAD-CHAR that two groups define, an undefined name, and the subscripted and reference-modified forms PAD-TAB (2) and PAD-LONG (2:1), which SR2 does not permit (§1985:III.2: 'data-name' is "a word which must not be reference-modified, subscripted, or qualified unless specifically permitted by the rules of the format"), all compile and run. The clause has no run-time function here (no block padding on the host's files), so the harm is acceptance of nonconforming source only.

next.reason: 1985 VII.2.7.3 SR2: PADDING CHARACTER 'Data-name-1 may be qualified.' The PADDING CHARACTER clause does not exist in 2023: the file control entry formats and clauses of §2023:12.4.5 contain no PADDING clause and the word PADDING is not a 2023 reserved word (deleted by the 2014 edition, docs/VERSION_CHANGE_REFERENCE.md row 7.20). With the clause gone, the rule on its operand has no 2023 counterpart.
